evidence.notes: Furthest horizontal distance; much better block advantage when spaced at max range; 2nd hit active frames 1-9 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first hit whiffs, it connects on the 2nd to last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+4 on block); if the 1st hit is crouch blocked, opponent cannot switch to stand block the 2nd hit; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last 6 active frames connect, or 623MP / SA2 if the final active frame connects); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; Sweet Spot occurs when juggling into the 3rd or 4th active frame, dealing 1300 damage (single hit) with a higher spinning juggle launch (ensures a follow-up juggle is possible even midscreen); the 2nd hit's extended Knee hitbox is too high to connect on standing characters on active frames 2-7 (tall characters: active frames 4-6); sets up corner safe jump in certain juggle scenarios (e.g. after juggled 2MP~HP)

evidence.name: OD Tiger Knee Crush
evidence.notes: 1st hit transitions to a different follow-up on hit, resulting in higher damage and a tumbling +66 knockdown (allows a 623LP juggle in the corner); if 1st hit whiffs, the next 2 hits deal 500 damage each and give a worse knockdown (only 1 hit at farthest ranges); safe on block but usually lands inside the opponent's throw range; 2nd hit active frames 2-10 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out, it connects on the last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+1 on block); unlike HK Knee, the opponent can switch to stand block after the first hit connects, leaving Sagat at -2; blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; later hits put opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP)

evidence.name: LK Tiger Knee Crush
evidence.notes: Shortest horizontal distance; no front leg hurtbox on frames 10-12 (helps avoid low pokes); 3f extra landing recovery when absorbed by armor; much better block advantage (up to +2) when spaced at max range; active frames 2-10 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first active frame whiffs, it always connects on the last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+2 on block, 623LP juggle on hit); puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last active frame connects); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; can be whiffed in some situations for a side switch vs. knocked down opponents

evidence.name: MK Tiger Knee Crush
evidence.notes: Medium horizontal distance; no front leg hurtbox on frames 14-15 (helps avoid low pokes); 3f extra landing recovery when absorbed by armor; much better block advantage (up to +3) when spaced at max range; active frames 2-9 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first active frame whiffs, it connects on the 2nd to last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+2 on block, 623LP juggle on hit); puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last 4 active frames connect); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; can be whiffed in some situations for a side switch vs. knocked down opponents; sets up midscreen safe jump in certain juggle scenarios (e.g. after juggled 2MP~HP)

evidence.name: HP Tiger Uppercut
evidence.notes: Extremely long range but slow startup (cannot combo naturally from light normals, but works well as a combo ender from 5LK whiff punish); deals 600 less damage on active frames 3-10; cannot hit cross-up; can be charged into a much stronger version by holding the button 24 frames; releasing the button early results in uncharged 623HP with 8f startup after release; if partially charged, the Air Invuln is 1-9f then 1-11f after the button is released, and the airborne frames are 12-57f after the button is released; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-2 only)

evidence.name: HP Tiger Uppercut (Hold)
evidence.notes: Button must be held 24f for fully charged version; causes a wall splat on hit that leaves Sagat at a fixed distance (no follow-up combo); deals 1100 less damage on active frames 4-10 with no wallsplat animation (KD +29 on active frame 4); cannot hit cross-up; 1st hit puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-3 only)

evidence.name: HP Burning Knuckle
evidence.notes: Travels about 80% of the screen; can be spaced to be plus on block from farther ranges (causing a screen shake); good approach tool vs. opponents in Burnout, but no screen shake when +1~4 vs. Burnout; useful approach when following behind Power Wave; Terry raises his hands for a reactable visual cue; only cancelable on active frames 1-5 (cannot cancel on a farther range connect); puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state (can juggle after very late connect)

evidence.name: LK Crack Shoot
evidence.notes: First 2 active frames can only hit airborne opponents (functionally 18f startup); cannot hit cross-up; causes spike knockdown vs. airborne opponents; causes Hard Knockdown on Punish Counter (prevents follow-up links); can hop over many grounded attacks (especially crouching); can be used for a sideswitch mid-combo or a corpse hop on downed opponents; very strong vs. Burnout, dealing chip while staying close range with frame advantage

evidence.name: MK Crack Shoot
evidence.notes: 2 hits vs. airborne, 1 hit vs. grounded (different damage values accordingly); first 5 active frames can only hit airborne opponents (functionally 22f startup); cannot hit cross-up; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; causes Hard Knockdown on Counter-hit/Punish Counter (prevents follow-up links); can hop over many grounded attacks (even some standing); can be used for a sideswitch mid-combo or a corpse hop on downed opponents; very strong vs. Burnout, dealing chip while staying close range with frame advantage

evidence.name: HK Power Charge
evidence.notes: Farthest travel distance; cancelable on frames 26-45 into special moves (except Power Charge) on hit only; delaying the special cancel allows different conversions or more optimal damage; puts opponent into limited juggle state (airborne opponents are not launched as high, resulting in more limited follow-ups); only combos naturally from the first hit of 5HP

evidence.name: OD Power Charge
evidence.notes: Causes Wall Bounce on hit; cancelable on frames 20-39 into special moves (except Power Charge) on hit only (useful for midscreen positioning or keeping opponent cornered after wall bounce); if used twice in a combo, 2nd hit will cause a quick wall splat that drops straight to the ground; KD advantage varies based on distance from wall (farther away gives higher advantage); wall bounce may not come out after a delayed cancel into 214K (can scroll the screen forward to prevent the opponent from hitting the wall)

evidence.name: LK Power Charge
evidence.notes: Short travel distance; comboable from lights except 5LP; keeps opponent standing for strike/throw mixup on hit; can be spaced out to allow a follow-up combo on hit; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state

evidence.name: MK Power Charge
evidence.notes: Medium travel distance; comboable from 2MP or heavy normals; puts opponent into limited juggle state (airborne opponents are launched higher than the HK version); can juggle SA1 anywhere on screen; final 4 recovery frames are cancelable into SA2 on hit, allowing a juggle anywhere on screen; sets up a safe jump setup on a close range grounded hit

evidence.name: MP Power Wave
evidence.notes: 1-hit projectile; travels more quickly than LP version but dissipates at ~60% screen distance; causes knockdown on Counter-hit/Punish Counter (KD +33~46); hitbox is at ground level but reaches high enough to clash with standard projectiles; projectile speed starts slow and accelerates each active frame; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; no head hurtbox on frames 11-41 (while leaning over); extended arm hurtbox on frames 21-39 is projectile invuln

evidence.name: LP Rising Tackle
evidence.notes: Very short horizontal range (hits straight above Terry to anti-air close jumps); cannot hit cross-up; active frames 3-10 do reduced damage; only 1st active frame is cancelable (cancel may be impossible in combos from too far away); puts opponent into limited juggle state (allows follow-up juggles on a high connect)

evidence.name: Linya ng Liwanag
evidence.notes: Requires SA2 install; each use consumes 375f (25%) of SA2 install timer; deals Drive Damage on normal hit (0.5 bars if both hits connect); reaches fullscreen and extends a huge proximity guard hitbox from frame 15 onward; if the 1st hit is blocked, parried, or absorbed by armor, Yasmine stops her forward movement and does not perform the 2nd hit (this hit has 2f active + 24f recovery); on hit, Yasmine will dash behind the opponent (even in the corner) and perform a 2nd hit that launches the opponent into a limited juggle state; this cross-up hit can also occur if the first hit whiffs (like in a knockdown setup or on a jumping opponent); cross-up hit has functionally 30f startup when used as an oki tool; can be canceled into from 2MK~HK and 5MK~MK~HK Target Combos on hit; active frame distribution is 2(11)5 when both hits connect; whiff recovery is 1f faster (19f) if Yasmine passes far behind the opponent before the 2nd hit comes out; startup time can be up to 3f faster (19f) if Yasmine passes through a close range airborne/teleporting opponent with no collision box; after a corner sideswitch, some follow-up juggles can whiff under the opponent (623HK requires delay, while 623MK and SA1 are auto-timed)

evidence.name: HP Talim ng Hangin
evidence.notes: Puts Yasmine into Bayani Mode on hit (this occurs after the hitstop of the 1st hit ends, so it will be granted when Super canceled but not if it trades with opponent's attack); plus on block advancing special; slow startup makes it reactable and only combos naturally from 2HP; last 2 hits only play out on hit and are not cancelable (listed recovery refers to the blocked/whiffed version); puts opponents into a limited juggle state (follow-ups only possible when juggled on airborne opponents)

evidence.name: MP Talim ng Hangin
evidence.notes: Puts Yasmine into Bayani Mode on hit (this occurs after the hitstop of the 1st hit ends, so it will be granted when Super canceled but not if it trades with opponent's attack); safe on block advancing special; last 2 hits only play out on hit and are not cancelable (listed recovery refers to the blocked version); 3f extra recovery on whiff; 4f extra recovery when absorbed by armor (guaranteed punish when absorbed by Drive Impact unless canceled into SA3); counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage carries through both hits (gives light confirms on CH and medium confirms on PC); puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (follow-ups are usually only possible in the corner)

evidence.name: Pangil sa Likuran
evidence.notes: 2-hit boomerang projectile (can only hit once on the way up, then applies all remaining hits on the way back); button strength determines projectile distance (LP short / MP mid / HP far); the listed active frames are for the L/M/H versions respectively; projectile disappears if Yasmine is hit; can only have one boomerang on-screen at a time; only the first 3 active frames are Super cancelable; the initial upward hit keeps opponents grounded (less range vs. crouching opponents); the returning projectile puts opponents into a limited juggle state; canceling from 2HP gives increased hit advantage (use LP boomerang from point blank 2HP for a link into 2LP in the corner); projectile speed refers to the initial activation before changing directions

evidence.name: OD Pangil sa Likuran
evidence.notes: 3-hit boomerang projectile (can only hit once on the way up, then applies all remaining hits on the way back); button combination determines projectile distance (LP+MP short / LP+HP mid / MP+HP far); the listed active frames are for the L/M/H versions respectively; projectile disappears if Yasmine is hit; can only have one boomerang on-screen at a time; only the first 3 active frames are Super cancelable; the initial upward hit keeps opponents grounded (less range vs. crouching opponents); the returning projectile puts opponents into a limited juggle state; canceling from 2HP gives increased hit advantage (use LP+MP boomerang from point blank 2HP for a link into 5LK); projectile speed refers to the initial activation before changing directions; the 2nd hit Juggle Limit depends on whether the 1st hit connected on the way up (if returning projectile has all 3 hits: JL 2,2,10; if only 2 hits on the returning projectile, JL 2 followed by JL 10,10); SA2 cancel: +16/+12

evidence.name: HP Daloy ng Tubig
evidence.notes: Longest range and slowest startup (combos from 2MP, 2HP, and 5HP); too slow to frame trap when canceled into without Burnout or Drive Rush starter (always punishable in cancels, but if spaced in neutral can be safe to some stronger 6-frame punishes); leads to Alon follow-up that launches the opponent upward for midscreen oki or corner juggles (stronger juggles possible on enhanced follow-up); always a true blockstring when canceled into Alon follow-up

evidence.name: Mukha ng Langit
evidence.notes: Button strength determines trajectory (LK short, MK mid, HK far); cannot be steered manually after activation; follow-ups can be input starting on frame 24, and as late as frame 45 (236LK) / frame 42 (236MK) / frame 43 (236HK); can input OD follow-up with PP or KK for 2 Drive bars (safer on block); empty HK flip can have 1f longer or shorter aerial animation when crossing over the opponent at certain ranges; Yasmine is in a standing state with a standing-sized hurtbox during landing recovery

evidence.name: OD Mukha ng Langit
evidence.notes: Enhances the properties of follow-up attacks (improved hit and block advantage, can be input with no extra meter cost); can be steered by holding back/neutral/forward before the follow-up starts (no input gives the same trajectory as 236LK); gives more freedom to control Yasmine's trajectory compared to the meterless flip; follow-ups can be input on frames 24-46; Yasmine is in a standing state with a standing-sized hurtbox during landing recovery

evidence.name: OD Kulog
evidence.notes: Button strength determines downward trajectory (LK short, MK mid, HK far); can no longer alter the trajectory of OD Flip once the follow-up is activated; can be input with KK from a meterless Flip (button combination affects trajectory with LK+MK / LK+HK / MK+HK); cannot hit cross-up; stalls mid-air to bait anti-airs; plus on block and links into 5MP/2MP in almost all cases (worst advantage is only possible by inputting the follow-up right before landing against a point blank opponent); puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state

evidence.name: OD Ulan
evidence.notes: Cross-up only (in very ambiguous situations, can actually be blocked either direction before landing behind the opponent); button combination determines downward trajectory (LP+MP short / LP+HP mid / MP+HP far); can no longer alter the trajectory of OD Flip once the follow-up is activated; can use KD +42 safe jump setups to auto-time the deepest possible hit midscreen (may require OD Flip starter if the opponent Back Rises); puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (opponent falls toward Yasmine for easy follow-up)

evidence.name: Kulog

evidence.name: Ulan

evidence.name: LP Daloy ng Tubig
evidence.notes: Shortest range but fastest startup (combos from all light normals and fast enough to juggle in situations where MP/HP versions are too slow); frame traps when canceled from 2LP or 5LK (nearly always punishable, but when spaced may avoid strong 6-frame punishes); leads to Alon follow-up that keeps opponent grounded (enhanced follow-up gives a knockdown); always a true blockstring when canceled into Alon follow-up; with Alon, this version deals more damage than MP Daloy with less combo scaling (can be more useful in short combo routes)

evidence.name: LP Alon (Bayani)
evidence.notes: Spends the Bayani Mode enhancement; Yasmine performs the final hit on block unlike the standard version (safe on block and deals more Drive Damage); decent pressure tool vs. Burnout that deals more chip damage than the other versions (but opponent can walk back to avoid throws and prevent a 2LK chain from comboing); puts opponents into a limited juggle state (can only cancel into SA3 on grounded opponents, but in juggles like after 5MP~MP it can lead to a corner 623LK follow-up); grounded hit gives a KD +42 safe jump anywhere on the screen; always a true blockstring from Daloy ng Tubig starter; deals 0.1 bars of Drive Damage on a normal hit during SA2 Bayani Mode install

evidence.name: MP Daloy ng Tubig
evidence.notes: Medium range and startup (combos from mediums and 5LP~LP TC); frame traps when canceled from 5LP~LP, 5MP~MP, or 2MK (always punishable at this range, but if spaced in neutral can be safe to some stronger 6-frame punishes); leads to Alon follow-up that knocks down with good midscreen oki (OTG bounce juggles possible from enhanced follow-up); always a true blockstring when canceled into Alon follow-up

evidence.name: MP Alon (Bayani)
evidence.notes: Spends the Bayani Mode enhancement; Yasmine performs the final hit on block unlike the standard version (safe on block and deals more Drive Damage); decent pressure tool vs. Burnout (but opponent can walk back to avoid throws and prevent a 2LK chain from comboing); puts opponents into a limited juggle OTG Bounce state (can juggle into 623MK/KK, but in juggles like after 5MP~MP it bounces higher for a juggle into 5HP / 623HK / SA1); grounded hit gives a KD +42 safe jump anywhere on the screen (but this sacrifices the juggle follow-up damage); always a true blockstring from Daloy ng Tubig starter; deals 0.1 bars of Drive Damage on a normal hit during SA2 Bayani Mode install

evidence.name: OD Daloy ng Tubig
evidence.notes: Has the startup of the LP version with improved range and juggle potential for consistency; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle OTG bounce state (ensures OD Alon follow-up connects); safe on block and +1 in Burnout for continued pressure; leads to solid damage and corner carry; canceling directly into SA2 on block causes high pushback for weak pressure (always better to cancel from Alon follow-up); the OD follow-up plays out a cinematic cutscene that can lead to juggles if SA2 canceled; always a true blockstring when canceled into Alon follow-up; SA2 cancel: +9/+8

evidence.name: Double Lariat
evidence.notes: First hit can anti-air but cannot hit cross-ups; head hurtbox disappears on frames 1-5 of startup, then further shrinks hurtbox on frames 6-16; all hits (except 1st) whiff vs. crouch (only connects once on hit); can hold left/right to move during animation; cancel into SA3 is only useful vs. armor; final hit puts opponent into free juggle state (useful combo starter after stun); canceling into Lariat causes Zangief to move forward more quickly and expands the 2nd hit's lower hitbox for combo consistency

evidence.name: Double Lariat
evidence.notes: First hit can anti-air but cannot hit cross-ups; head hurtbox disappears on frames 1-5 of startup, then further shrinks hurtbox on frames 6-13; can hold left/right to move during animation; connects twice on hit, 5 times vs. stand block (true blockstring), or 3 times vs. crouch block (1f gap between final 2 hits if not in Burnout); fairly strong chip-out tool on burned out opponents (high pushback on block makes it very difficult for most characters to punish when the final hit is spaced out); 1st hit crumples grounded opponents (allows SA3 combo); faster startup makes it more consistent than meterless Lariat in combos; in juggles, can combo into j.360+KK or SA1 if the juggling hits are staggered; 1st active frame of 2nd hit only connects on grounded opponents
